signals.source_text: But slowly, in the spaces between calculations, he began to hear what Torrhen had been talking about.
The air had currents that moved according to temperature differentials and pressure gradients, but also according to subtler forces that his mathematical mind had never thought to measure.
But when he finally managed it—when his consciousness expanded beyond his bio-form and touched the crystalline awareness that dwelled within the ice—the experience was revelatory.
It remembered the water it had once been, the snow it had been before that, the vapor rising from oceans that had existed before Nibiru's shadow changed everything.
It remembered the water it had once been, the snow it had been before that, the vapor rising from oceans that had existed before Nibiru's shadow changed everything.

It held within its crystalline matrix the patterns of every droplet that had contributed to its formation, the history of weather systems spanning millennia, the quantum memories of molecular interactions that stretched back to the birth of the world itself.
Not melting—the temperature remained far below any threshold that would permit phase change.

Structures that served functional purposes—improved thermal retention, enhanced acoustic resonance, greater structural stability—but achieved those purposes through beauty rather than mere efficiency.
He felt changed on some fundamental level, as if the boundary between his mathematical mind and the external world had been permanently altered.
